transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-30 10:00 PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Leo (CSM), Alex (CTO), Priya (ML), Samir (SRE), Nina (Product)

Summary auto-gen (may be rough): cost econ review, caching numbers, batching tuning, plan next benchmarks

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — recap last week's runs, cost model updates, caching results, batching tradeoffs, and next steps. does that look right to folks?
00:10 Alex: yeah that's good — we wanna make sure the tokens per dollar numbers line up with our internal numbers, we saw a gap last time.
00:18 Maya: yeah so we re-ran the suite with the newer quantize profile and updated kernel selection. rough headline: tokens/sec per dollar improved ~18% on the 2k seq workload vs last week bc of better batching + quantization mix. caveat: 99p latency shifted a bit due to bigger batches.
00:35 Priya: when you say quantize mix, is that the int8 path or the mixed float16 path? we recall mixed gave better quality for our retrieval use case.
00:40 Maya: right — for the retrieval rerank flows we kept mixed-fp16 for the topK to avoid quality regressions, and used int8 for the generative fallback path. that's in the spreadsheet I uploaded, the assumptions tab has quality deltas.
01:02 Samir: can you repeat the tokens/sec/$ number? our finance team needs that number normalized to cloud cost.
01:10 Maya: sure — normalized tokens per dollar is 3.2M tokens per dollar for the baseline hosted config with caching off; with caching on for the top-50 prefixes we see effective tokens/sec/$ of about 4.1M — so roughly a 28% effective cost decrease for that workload. note that's workload dependent.
01:35 Alex: 28% is great, is that mostly prefix caching KV saving or is batching contributing?
01:42 Maya: good q — split is approx 18% from KV/prefix caching and ~8-10% from continuous batching improvements given the request mix. the remaining difference is from the quantization kernel selection.
02:05 Nina: are those caching numbers from Redwood Hosted or Dedicated? curious if private deployment affects that.
02:12 Maya: these are hosted runs but the caching layer is consistent across deployments. on Dedicated, you'd see similar or slightly better savings bc the runtime can reserve bigger KV cache sizes and avoid noisy neighbor issues. but dedicated has committed cost so the per-token math changes — we'll model that in the spreadsheet.
02:40 Jordan: quick note on dedicated economics — for short pilots Dedicated can look more expensive per-day due to commitment but gives predictable throughput and often better tail latency once tuned.
02:52 Priya: we care a lot about 99p latency — our user-facing app can't have big tail spikes. you mentioned the 99p worsened, how much?
03:00 Maya: on the 2k seq generative path 99p moved from ~820ms to ~1,100ms when we increased batch target from 8 to 16 to hit higher tokens/sec. median stayed around 120-140ms. so higher throughput but larger tails.
03:25 Samir: that's not acceptable for the main UI, maybe fine for async jobs. can we do dynamic batching or latency SLO routing?
03:33 Maya: yes — Redwood supports policy-based routing: low-latency path (smaller batch target) vs high-throughput path. we can split by route or by caller metadata. we demoed that earlier, but for the POC we can configure 80/20 split to keep UI on low-latency.
03:55 Alex: what's the cost hit if we keep 80/20 low latency?
04:00 Maya: ballpark you'd lose ~6-9% of tokens/sec/$ vs fully optimized high-throughput, but 99p latency for UI route returns to ~900ms or lower depending on model. exact numbers in sheet.
04:18 Priya: about caching — we sent top-100 prefixes last week, did you use those? we also have user sessions where prefixes change often.
04:26 Maya: we used your top-100 sample; caching hit-rate was ~46% on that set. we estimate diminishing returns after top-200. also noted that session variability reduces cache efficacy for some flows.
04:40 Priya: any automatic prefix suggestion tooling?
04:43 Maya: we have a suggestions CLI and the optimize recommendations in Console — it suggests which prefixes to materialize based on real traffic. I'll include the CLI output in the spreadsheet.
04:58 Jordan: any security concerns with caching? Alex?
05:03 Alex: since prefixes can contain PII in some flows, we need to ensure KMS encryption at rest and audit logs for cache access. does Redwood's cache respect customer KMS?
05:12 Maya: yes — cache snapshot and store can be encrypted with customer KMS in Private/Dedicated; on Hosted we encrypt at rest and can do bring-your-key for Dedicated/Private. we'll attach the security note.
05:30 Samir: good — add audit logs to the action items.
05:35 Leo: noted.
05:40 Maya: back to batching tradeoffs — we can do adaptive batching based on latency SLOs per route. also can set max batch age which helps limit tail latency while gaining batching benefits. the spreadsheet has those knobs and a simulated cost curve.
06:05 Priya: can you remind us how batching affects token accounting? like tokens/sec/$ metrics — is it per-GPU or normalized across the cluster?
06:14 Maya: we normalize to tokens per dollar across the instance pool, factoring in utilization and amortized infra. so when we say 3.2M tokens/$ that's across the serving pool with the run config. if you provision Dedicated with lower utilization variability, effective tokens/$ can go up.
06:35 Alex: what's the plan for the 99p benchmark run you mentioned?
06:40 Maya: propose we run a dedicated benchmark on a small dedicated pool next Wednesday — full production traffic replay with 99p capture. need Samir to provision the VPC and Priya to provide prompt distribution. we'll also test split routing 80/20 and adaptive batching.
06:58 Samir: I can put up a test VPC, need a runbook for network egress and security groups.
07:03 Maya: I'll send the runbook and a checklist.
07:10 Jordan: ok, procurement question — if we go Dedicated pilot for 3 months what's the pricing?
07:16 Jordan: (continues) typical pilot pricing is a short-term commit with lower UoM; I'll share options: monthly reserved with option to convert, and a usage overage model. I'll send formal pricing.
07:30 Alex: we may also evaluate Anthropic for a subset of calls — just to benchmark. any gotchas?
07:36 Maya: Anthropic's instrumentation is different; their batch behavior and kernel stack vary. we can include a side-by-side but may not be identical configs. it's useful for high-level cost/comparison but not apples-to-apples.
07:54 Priya: any quality regressions from quantization? our tests found a 0.7% hit on rerank accuracy for int8 on some queries.
07:59 Maya: yes we measured similar and flagged it. that's why we kept mixed-fp16 for rerank and int8 for the less-sensitive generation. quality deltas are documented in the 'quality' tab.
08:15 Nina: final question on observability — can we see token-level cost by route and by prompt template?
08:22 Maya: yes Console has per-route token breakdown and trace links; we can add a custom dashboard for your top templates.
08:30 Jordan: wrap up — recap action items and owners.
08:35 Alex: thanks all.

Transcript notes: occasional automated timestamps and speaker attribution imperfect. Some product names transcribed as Redwood Dedicate or K V cache in interim notes.

End of transcript.
